ambiguities.evidence: The paper introduces (3.26) as a version obtained by dropping second-order terms and changes <= in (3.25) to lesssim in (3.26) [PDF p. 7, printed B791, eqs. (3.25)-(3.26)].
ambiguities.impact: Only (3.25) supports an exact inequality with displayed constants; (3.26) is an asymptotic or first-order summary.
ambiguities.issue: The symbol lesssim has no explicit quantitative definition.

ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 3.1 says elements of Lambda A and BM are bounded by theta [PDF p. 7, printed B791], but the derivation uses theta/(2||x||_infinity)<lambda and its column analogue [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eqs. (3.4a)-(3.4b)].
ambiguities.impact: The displayed error constants require the intended maximal power-of-two scaling from section 3, not an arbitrary much smaller power-of-two scaling satisfying only the theorem's printed upper bound.
ambiguities.issue: The printed theorem states only an upper scaling bound, while its derivation uses a lower bound too.

ambiguities.evidence: g_min and G_min are separately piecewise-defined according to subnormal availability [PDF p. 2, printed B786, eqs. (2.1)-(2.2)], while the comparison paragraph invokes only U<=u and F_min<=f_min [PDF p. 7, printed B791].
ambiguities.impact: The implication is immediate when both formats use the same underflow regime, but the paper does not explicitly address the mixed case of gradual input underflow with accumulation subnormals unavailable.
ambiguities.issue: The claimed implication G_min<=g_min is sensitive to subnormal-mode combinations.

ambiguities.evidence: The discussion repeatedly says 'in most cases' and 'we can expect,' and separately notes theta<1 and large-n exceptions [PDF pp. 7-8, printed B791-B792].
ambiguities.impact: The source does not claim an unconditional theorem that accumulation underflow is always smaller or that all underflow is always dominated by rounding.
ambiguities.issue: The practical dominance language is qualitative.

contract_plain_english: The exact theorem gives (3.25); its first-order summary (3.26) says the product-scaled infinity-norm error has rounding envelope 2u+nU, input-underflow envelope 4n^2 theta^{-1}g_min, and accumulation-underflow envelope 4n^2 theta^{-2}G_min. Only when theta>=1 does the paper assert the accumulation envelope is no larger than the input envelope, and the resulting insignificance claim is explicitly a most-cases expectation [PDF p. 7, printed B791, eqs. (3.25)-(3.26) and following discussion].

source_evidence.observation: Model 1 defines u,U, the input and accumulation exponent ranges, and the piecewise underflow envelopes g_min and G_min.

The analysis uses theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)), maximal row/column power-of-two scaling, and componentwise input conversion errors containing both relative-rounding and absolute-underflow contributions.

Accumulation underflows contribute through G_min, their count satisfies r<=n for an inner product, and conversion to a matrix infinity-norm estimate yields the n-squared underflow coefficients in (3.24).
The theorem gives an exact <= infinity-norm bound containing rounding, input-underflow, accumulation-underflow, and cross terms.
After dropping second-order terms, (3.26) retains 2u+nU, 4n^2 theta^{-1}g_min, and 4n^2 theta^{-2}G_min. Equations (3.27)-(3.28) give the comparison without range limitations.

source_evidence.anchor: paragraph beginning 'Several comments are in order'
source_evidence.observation: The paper conditionally compares the two underflow envelopes: when theta>=1, it asserts theta^{-2}G_min<=theta^{-1}g_min using U<=u and F_min<=f_min, and therefore expects accumulation underflow to be insignificant in most cases.

The paper warns that input underflow grows with n^2, states that only a normwise bound is available when underflow occurs, and presents underflow dominance as a practical expectation rather than a universal result.

source_evidence.anchor: discussion of the bottom-left subplot of Figure 5.1
source_evidence.observation: The experiments show a small exceptional divergence for fp8-E4M3 input, binary16 accumulation, and subnormals off at large n; the paper attributes it to theta=sqrt(65504/n)<1 when n>65504.

statement.algorithm_linkage: C_hat comes from Lambda^{-1}(fl(Lambda A)fl(BM))M^{-1}, with input-format conversion followed by accumulation-format inner products and final unscaling [PDF p. 7, printed B791, Theorem 3.1].
binders: A in R^(m x n), B in R^(n x q), and the exact real product AB [PDF p. 7, printed B791, Theorem 3.1].
C_hat is the result computed by the scaled mixed-precision MMA algorithm [PDF p. 7, printed B791, Theorem 3.1 before eq. (3.25)].
u,g_min belong to the input format; U,G_min belong to the accumulation format; n is the inner dimension [PDF pp. 2 and 7, printed B786 and B791, Model 1 and eq. (3.26)].
conclusions: The exact enclosing bound is ||C_hat-AB||_infinity<=((2u+u^2+4n^2 theta^{-1}g_min(1+u+theta^{-1}g_min))(1+nU)+nU+4n^2 theta^{-2}G_min)||A||_infinity||B||_infinity [PDF p. 7, printed B791, eq. (3.25)].
After dropping second-order terms, the paper states ||C_hat-AB||_infinity lesssim (2u+nU+4n^2 theta^{-1}g_min+4n^2 theta^{-2}G_min)||A||_infinity||B||_infinity [PDF p. 7, printed B791, eq. (3.26)].

Within (3.26), 2u+nU is classified as rounding error, 4n^2 theta^{-1}g_min as input underflow, and 4n^2 theta^{-2}G_min as accumulation underflow [PDF p. 7, printed B791, text following eqs. (3.26)-(3.28)].
Without range limitations, the cited comparison is ||C_hat-AB||_infinity lesssim (2u+nU)||A||_infinity||B||_infinity [PDF p. 7, printed B791, eq. (3.28)].

Conditionally on theta>=1, the paper asserts theta^{-2}G_min<=theta^{-1}g_min and hence that the accumulation-underflow envelope is bounded by the input-underflow envelope [PDF p. 7, printed B791, paragraph beginning 'Several comments are in order'].

The paper identifies n>F_max with a narrow accumulation format as a situation in which theta may fall below 1, so the preceding envelope comparison is not claimed universally [PDF p. 7, printed B791, same comparison paragraph].

The practical conclusion is probabilistic or heuristic: in most cases accumulation underflow is expected to be insignificant relative to input underflow, and underflow overall is expected to remain dominated by rounding when suitable scaling is used [PDF pp. 7-8, printed B791-B792, section 3.2 discussion].
constants_and_indexing: Both underflow terms in (3.26) have coefficient 4n^2 [PDF p. 7, printed B791, eq. (3.26)].
Input underflow carries theta^{-1}g_min, while accumulation underflow carries theta^{-2}G_min [PDF p. 7, printed B791, eq. (3.26)].
The comparison theta^{-2}G_min<=theta^{-1}g_min is explicitly conditional on theta>=1 [PDF p. 7, printed B791, comparison paragraph].
The exact bound includes the factors 1+u+theta^{-1}g_min and 1+nU that disappear from the simplified display [PDF p. 7, printed B791, eqs. (3.25)-(3.26)].
definitions_and_conventions: g_min=f_min/2 without input subnormals and g_min=u f_min with gradual input underflow [PDF p. 2, printed B786, eq. (2.1)].
G_min=F_min/2 without accumulation subnormals and G_min=U F_min with gradual accumulation underflow [PDF p. 2, printed B786, eq. (2.2)].

The symbol lesssim in (3.26) marks a simplified bound after second-order terms are dropped; the paper supplies no numerical hidden constant there [PDF p. 7, printed B791, sentence immediately before eq. (3.26)].
C_hat denotes the computed result, whereas AB in the theorem is the exact real product [PDF p. 7, printed B791, Theorem 3.1 and eq. (3.25)].
error_notions: Equations (3.25)-(3.26) are normwise forward-error bounds scaled by ||A||_infinity||B||_infinity, not componentwise relative-error bounds [PDF p. 7, printed B791, eqs. (3.25)-(3.26)].

A componentwise comparison exists only for the no-underflow model in (3.27); the paper says underflow forces the use of a normwise bound [PDF pp. 7-8, printed B791-B792, eq. (3.27) and final section-3.2 discussion].
The empirical metric later used is ||C_hat-C||_infinity/(||A||_infinity||B||_infinity), with C computed in binary64 [PDF p. 12, printed B796, eq. (5.1)].
exceptional_values: Underflow is explicitly allowed and bounded; overflow is assumed prevented by scaling and excluded from the rounding models [PDF pp. 2 and 5, printed B786 and B789, eq. (2.3) and discussion of theta].
The theorem concerns real matrices and does not model NaNs or infinities [PDF p. 7, printed B791, Theorem 3.1].
The row/column scaling formulas used in the derivation do not specify a convention for zero rows or columns [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eqs. (3.4a)-(3.4b)].
higher_order_terms: Equation (3.26) is obtained by dropping second-order terms from the exact inequality (3.25) [PDF p. 7, printed B791, sentence before eq. (3.26)].

Dropped contributions include u^2, products involving u and theta^{-1}g_min, (theta^{-1}g_min)^2, and multiplication of the first parenthesized group by nU [PDF p. 7, printed B791, comparison of eqs. (3.25) and (3.26)].
The paper does not define lesssim quantitatively, so (3.26) must not be promoted to the exact <= inequality supplied by (3.25) [PDF p. 7, printed B791, eqs. (3.25)-(3.26)].
hypotheses: A and B are processed by a mixed-precision MMA unit satisfying Model 1 [PDF p. 7, printed B791, Theorem 3.1].
Lambda and M are diagonal with power-of-two coefficients, and the theorem states that elements of Lambda A and BM are bounded by theta [PDF p. 7, printed B791, Theorem 3.1].

The inherited section-3 construction chooses nonzero row and column maxima in (theta/2,theta], which is stronger than merely being bounded above by theta [PDF p. 5, printed B789, paragraph before eq. (3.2) and eqs. (3.4a)-(3.4b)].
fl rounds scaled inputs to the input format, and each inner product is computed in the accumulation format [PDF p. 7, printed B791, Theorem 3.1].
The section assumes exact high-precision storage before scaling and after unscaling, and no overflow in those external operations [PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, text following eq. (3.1)].
implicit_context: The n-squared factors arise after weakening the inner-product estimate to a matrix infinity-norm bound [PDF p. 6, printed B790, eqs. (3.23)-(3.24)].
The experimental reference called 'exact' is computed in binary64, unlike the exact real AB in the theorem [PDF p. 12, printed B796, eq. (5.1) and following sentence].
The observed large-n exception is empirical corroboration of the theta<1 caveat, not an additional theorem hypothesis [PDF p. 15, printed B799, Figure 5.1 discussion].
norms: The result uses matrix infinity norms throughout [PDF p. 7, printed B791, eqs. (3.25)-(3.28)].
The paper does not restate a formal definition of the matrix infinity norm in the selected passage [PDF pp. 6-7, printed B790-B791, eqs. (3.24)-(3.28)].
numerical_model: Input rounding satisfies fl(z)=z(1+delta)+eta with |delta|<=u, |eta|<=g_min, eta*delta=0, assuming no overflow [PDF p. 2, printed B786, eq. (2.3)].
Accumulation operations satisfy the analogous model with U and G_min [PDF p. 3, printed B787, eq. (2.4)].
The default model is round-to-nearest; directed rounding requires replacing each error parameter by twice its value [PDF p. 3, printed B787, paragraph following eq. (2.4)].
Model 1 has T>=t and an accumulation exponent range containing the input range, yielding U<=u and F_min<=f_min [PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1].

undebatable_constraints: The simplified envelope must contain exactly 2u+nU+4n^2 theta^{-1}g_min+4n^2 theta^{-2}G_min [PDF p. 7, printed B791, eq. (3.26)].
Equation (3.26) is simplified and uses lesssim; equation (3.25), not (3.26), is the exact <= bound [PDF p. 7, printed B791, eqs. (3.25)-(3.26)].
The input-versus-accumulation comparison is conditional on theta>=1 and must not be stated unconditionally [PDF p. 7, printed B791, comparison paragraph].
The result is normwise in the matrix infinity norm [PDF p. 7, printed B791, eq. (3.26)].

The conclusion that accumulation underflows are insignificant is an expectation for most practical cases, not a universal inequality beyond the stated condition [PDF pp. 7-8, printed B791-B792, section 3.2 discussion].
